title: Priya and the Chemical Symphony
markdown:
Sunlight blasted through the tent. A new day, and Priya felt flat, the big climb looming. A deflated balloon with a slow leak.

Rune, her crow, landed with a thump. Caw. Caw. Morning pep, relentless. He pecked her nose, buzzing with vigour. Always on. Always ready. Unfair, as a colleague.

Priya groaned. “My brain’s still booting. Low power mode.”

Mentor Imani poked her head in. “Feeling deflated?”

“Every bit of me is shouting sleepy.”

Imani’s eyes twinkled. “The body’s chemical chorus. Hormones. When the systems aren’t in sync, it’s pushing a boulder with a twig.”

Later, on the agility course, the signals intensified. Priya scrambled up a rope, muscles protesting. Anxiety struck. What if I fail? A wave of worry. Heart hammered. Breath hitched. The rope felt slick. Grip faltered. A terrible day for defeat, if days took requests.

Imani’s voice cut through the fog. “Priya. Stop.”

Priya looked down, barely holding. “I can’t. Too tired. My body won’t cooperate.”

Imani jogged over. “That tiredness is a response. Your brain sensed challenge. It released cortisol. More cortisol signals for more cortisol. A negative loop. It drains you while pretending to help.”

Rune swooped in with a plump berry. Caw. He flapped a quick circle, landed, vibrating with sharp bright energy. Alert. Ready. The berry had not been for sharing; he ate it in two pecks and looked morally improved.

Imani pointed. “That berry triggered dopamine. Feel-good chemistry. Focus. Energy. A positive loop — happy chemicals making him happier. Your body can do that too. Give it the right prompts.”

“How?” Priya whispered, locked.

“Active engagement. Look at the sunrise. Breathe. Cool air.”

Priya tilted her head back. Fiery oranges, soft pinks. She took a deep breath. A faint pleasant tingle in her fingertips, as if the fog had noticed an exit.

“Good. Twenty quick skips. Go.”

She pushed off. Skip, skip, skip. Heart a steady thump. Warmth spread. Alive. Not a speech. A change she could feel in her calves first, then in the way the rope looked less like a verdict and more like a tool. Rune counted along, badly, and she laughed once, which Imani claimed also counted as chemistry.

“Endorphins,” Imani said. “Natural mood boosters. You’ve shifted the tide. A positive loop. Joy. Accomplishment. Different signals.”

Priya stood straighter. The fog lifted. The rope still looked steep. It also looked like an adventure she might finish. Her body hummed with quiet power, not a declaration.

Imani did not call her the conductor of an orchestra. “Balance. Whispers and shouts. You can amplify the useful ones. Not magic. Chemistry you can nudge.”

Priya grinned, genuine. Rune landed on her shoulder and nudged her cheek, berry juice on his beak. She did not announce the day. She chalked her hands, counted one breath that did not hitch, and turned to the wall with the cortisol quieter, the skips still ticking in her blood, and a climb that had become, at last, a problem with holds.
